requirement:
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.

The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
rationale:
The tests cover most of `requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`, but one obligation has no assertion: a file with no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such.

**What the tests cover**
- **Exact 80% threshold:** `exact_per_file_threshold_and_partial_functions` checks `threshold(79_999, 100_000)` fails and `threshold(80_000, 100_000)` passes. Rounding to 80.0% therefore does not pass. It also checks `threshold(0, 0)` fails.
- **Boundary at 4/5:** the same test checks that a file at 4/5 (80.0%) passes while containing a function that is only partly covered by lines. No 80% target is imposed per function.
- **No rescue across files:** it adds `driver.rs` at 0/1 beside a fully covered `code.rs`. The check fails and the output contains `driver.rs: 0/1 (0.0%)` and `uncovered lines: 1`. An aggregate or averaged percentage would not fail here.
- **Union rule:** `children_and_filtered_runs_contribute_to_the_same_union` unions a parent and a child process from one attempt, then adds a newer filtered test whose counts are all zero. It asserts the check still passes. This covers a location counting once, any positive count covering it, and a later zero not erasing earlier execution.
- **Unmeasured file:** `unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear` asserts `code.rs: not measured — FAIL` for a file with executable code and no recorded lines.
- **Absence of lines is not proof:** `default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not` calls `inventory` directly. A macro invocation or a `#[derive]` file does not count as having no executable obligations. A declaration-only file does.
- **Exemption from the threshold:** `unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear` asserts the check passes for a declaration-only file with no lines.
- **Parse failures:** the same test asserts a parse failure is reported rather than skipped.
- **Exceptions:** `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution` covers a file below the threshold with an accepted exception. It asserts `code.rs: 0/1 (0.0%) — accepted exception`. That test carries the `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions` marks, not the subject's.
- **Freshness, configuration and selection:** `stale_missing_legacy_and_uncertain_history_cannot_use_older_success` covers stale records, missing coverage, and another configuration being excluded. It carries the `check.measurement` mark, not the subject's. I treated it as acceptable context for those cited rules.

**Gap: "reported as such" is never asserted**
- The requirement says a file established to contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such, as well as not requiring an exception.
- `check_in` produces the label `no executable obligations` for this case.
- No test asserts it. The only test of this case, `unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear`, checks `report(root).passed` for the declaration-only `code.rs` and never inspects `result.text`. A search of the project finds that phrase only in `check_in` and in an assertion message string.
- An implementation that passed such a file silently, or labelled it `not measured` or with a fabricated percentage while still passing, would satisfy every reviewed assertion. That violates the "reported as such" clause and the ban on fabricating a percentage.

Because an obligation stated in the subject's text lacks an asserting test, and no `{fixme}` acknowledges it, the determination is false.

text: :::{req} check.threshold
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.
The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Search results are not evidence inputs under {cite}`requirements.authoring.text_search`, so only sources an assessment received as mandatory inputs or read count. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
:::{req} index.summary
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST identify the
contributing runs and show each selected test's binary, test name, attempt,
capture time, command, selection, and outcome, including missing or stale
coverage. It MUST show source revisions and uncommitted-source state when
available rather than present records from several runs as one run.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST link to {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.details`, visibly identify
incomplete coverage, and MUST NOT imply that every current test has coverage
merely because all available records are valid.
:::{req} index.selection
The coverage index MUST combine the most recent recorded test attempt for each
nextest binary and test name among the retained runs. "Most recent" MUST refer
to when the attempt started, including failed or interrupted attempts. A newer
filtered run MUST update only the tests it executes, leaving other compatible
test records available to the combined view. A newer attempt with missing or
unreadable coverage MUST be shown as unavailable rather than replaced with an
older successful attempt. Results from incompatible instrumented build
configurations MUST NOT be combined under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration`.
The main combined view MUST use the instrumented build configuration of the
most recently started recorded test attempt. Latest-per-test selection MUST
occur within that configuration. Records from other configurations MUST be
identified as excluded historical coverage. Configuration selection MUST use
recorded metadata without building or executing tests.
:::{req} index.freshness
Only records whose captured source inputs match the current project source and
whose build configurations are compatible MAY contribute execution counts to
the combined view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`.
Records invalidated by a source change, or whose compatibility cannot be
established, MUST be identified as stale or unavailable and excluded from the
combined coverage totals. Their retained per-process reports MUST remain
inspectable using their captured source until the build artifacts are removed.
